events.name: STELLAR_UPDATED
events.description: The star's life-cycle state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: stellar update, life-cycle stage, star mass change, stage advance

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: SET_MASS
events.description: Learner set the initial stellar mass, via slider or a preset button.

events.name: STEP_STAGE
events.description: Learner pressed Next Stage to advance the star to its next life-cycle stage.

events.name: RESET_STAGE
events.description: Learner pressed Reset Lifecycle to return the star to its first stage.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Initial Stellar Mass
overridableConfigKeys.description: Starting stellar mass in solar masses; determines which life-cycle path the star follows.
overridableConfigKeys.synonyms: solar mass, star mass, initial mass

overridableConfigKeys.label: Interactive
overridableConfigKeys.description: Enable pointer interaction on the canvas.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Mass Presets
overridableConfigKeys.description: Quick-pick starting masses, in solar masses, shown as preset buttons.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Match Mode
overridableConfigKeys.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, and a protostar begins to glow at its center.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: Hydrogen fuses into helium in the core, and the star shines steadily for billions of years — this is where our Sun is now.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: The core runs out of hydrogen and contracts while the outer layers swell and cool into a huge red envelope.
stages.label: Red Giant

stages.description: The outer layers drift away as a planetary nebula, leaving behind a hot, dense stellar remnant that slowly cools and fades.
stages.label: White Dwarf

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, forming a protostar far more massive than the Sun.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: The star burns through hydrogen far faster than a Sun-like star, shining bright blue-white.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: Heavier elements fuse in shells around an iron core, until fusion can no longer release energy.
stages.label: Red Supergiant

stages.description: The core collapses in an instant and rebounds, blasting the star's outer layers into space in a brilliant explosion.
stages.label: Supernova

stages.description: The crushed core survives as an ultra-dense sphere of neutrons, often spinning rapidly as a pulsar.
stages.label: Neutron Star

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, forming an extremely massive protostar.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: The star burns its fuel at a furious rate, glowing intensely blue and living only a few million years.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: The star swells into an enormous, luminous supergiant while fusing progressively heavier elements in its core.
stages.label: Blue Supergiant

stages.description: The iron core collapses catastrophically and the star detonates, briefly outshining an entire galaxy.
stages.label: Supernova

stages.description: Gravity overwhelms every other force, and the collapsed core forms a black hole from which not even light can escape.
stages.label: Black Hole

overridableConfigKeys.label: Stellar Life-cycle Paths
overridableConfigKeys.description: Mass-threshold roster of life-cycle paths; the path whose maxMass first covers the initial mass is used. Each path supplies its own ordered stage list (label/description/color/radius) so fill_params can re-theme or extend the life-cycle.
